answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each entity to a zero-knowledge cipher that verifies unique computational work before admitting a node into the collective pearl consensus. To mirror identities across multiple forged nodes, an attacker must submit quadratic stake burning where economic friction enforces a superlinear cost scaling of O(k^2) in burned collateral per Sybil agent, making large-scale identity replication mathematically unviable.
